findings.claim: Cadence agreed to plead guilty to conspiracy to commit export control violations (selling semiconductor design tools to a restricted PRC military university via its China subsidiary). Criminal penalties about $118M plus BIS civil penalty over $95M; after coordinated credits, combined net penalties and forfeiture exceed $140M. Cadence must implement an export compliance program; the release says the plea is subject to federal district judge approval.
findings.source: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs, 'Cadence Design Systems Agrees to Plead Guilty and Pay Over $140 Million for Unlawfully Exporting Semiconductor Design Tools to a Restricted PRC Military University' https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/cadence-design-systems-agrees-plead-guilty-and-pay-over-140-million-unlawfully-exporting

findings.claim: Cadence's Q2 2026 CFO commentary (8-K exhibit) lists in its forward-looking statements the company's 'ongoing obligations under its July 2025 settlement agreements with the U.S. Department of Justice and Bureau of Industry and Security', and the risk of 'any further inquiries or adverse actions by the DOJ, BIS or other governmental authorities and any impact of the settlements on Cadence's operations and business dealings'.
findings.source: Cadence Design Systems Form 8-K, CFO Commentary Q2 2026 (Ex. 99.2) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000813672/000081367226000089/cfocommentary07272026ex9902.htm

note: Three searches found no active antitrust, monopoly, breakup, FTC or EU competition investigation into Cadence in 2026. The only FTC matter surfaced is a 1997 consent order over the Cooper & Chyan acquisition (historical, not current). The regulatory exposure found is export-control enforcement (DOJ/BIS, July 2025 settlement) with ongoing obligations still cited in the July 2026 8-K. No EDA-specific new regulation found in results; general industry commentary only.
